title: Health insurance deduction (80D), HRA and home-loan interest — old regime deductions
publisher: Artha Kavach summary of public guidance (RBI / SEBI / IRDAI / Income Tax Dept) — pending manual verification
text: If you choose the old tax regime, three common deductions beyond 80C are: Section 80D — premiums paid for health insurance for yourself, spouse and children (up to about ₹25,000, higher for senior-citizen parents, and an additional amount for parents); HRA — if you pay rent and your salary has an HRA component, part of it is exempt, calculated as the least of actual HRA received, rent paid minus 10% of basic, and 50%/40% of basic depending on the city; and Section 24(b) — up to ₹2 lakh of interest on a self-occupied home loan. Keep rent receipts, the landlord's PAN if rent is above ₹1 lakh a year, and premium receipts. These are not available in the new regime, so compare both before deciding.
summary_hinglish: Old regime mein 80C ke alawa 80D (health insurance premium, ~₹25,000 tak, parents ke liye alag), HRA (rent par chhoot, rent receipts rakho) aur home loan interest 24(b) (₹2 lakh tak) milte hain. New regime mein ye nahi milte, isliye dono compare karo.
summary_hi: पुराने रिजीम में 80C के अलावा 80D (हेल्थ इंश्योरेंस प्रीमियम), HRA (किराये पर छूट) और 24(b) (होम लोन ब्याज, ₹2 लाख तक) की कटौती मिलती है। नए रिजीम में ये नहीं मिलतीं, इसलिए दोनों की तुलना करें।
aliases: 80d hra house rent allowance home loan interest 24b deductions health insurance premium
